header.headline: Eight modules, one clinical surface
header.subhead: KONSENXIA's feature set spans consultation, collaboration, learning, and records. Status for every module: architecture or roadmap unless a lab source says otherwise.

architecture.title: How the pieces fit
architecture.note: Source: repo docs/healthcare_ai_architecture.md; legal posture: docs/legal/*.

layers.title: Clinical engagement layer
layers.body: Consultation, differential diagnosis prompts, and emergency consult entry points presented in a single clinical workspace.

layers.title: Doctor-to-doctor layer
layers.body: Peer consultation channels that keep licensed clinicians in the decision path for every recommendation.

layers.title: Knowledge & analytics layer
layers.body: Knowledge hub retrieval, drug analytics, and medical file understanding — retrieval-augmented and document-grounded where possible.

layers.title: Anonymization pipeline
layers.body: Separates learning signals from direct identifiers before any use in anonymized learning. Designed for privacy; certification is a future milestone, not a current claim.

layers.title: Compliance & governance layer
layers.body: KVKK + GDPR design goals expressed in architecture and legal documentation; HIPAA-aligned handling as a target posture for qualifying deployments.

features.title: Feature modules
features.note: Status vocabulary: architecture (designed, documented) or roadmap (planned). No lab-validated numbers exist for these modules yet.

items.name: AI medical consultation
items.body: Structured consultation flow where the assistant gathers context, proposes considerations, and defers the clinical decision to the physician.

items.name: Doctor-to-doctor
items.body: Peer-to-peer consult between licensed clinicians, with the assistant summarising context rather than replacing judgement.

items.name: Anonymized learning
items.body: Continuous improvement loop fed by de-identified signals. "Designed for" anonymization — not certified — until audit evidence exists.

items.name: Differential diagnosis
items.body: Ranked differential prompts with explicit uncertainty, designed to widen — not close — the clinician's consideration set.

items.name: Emergency consult
items.body: Fast-path consultation for time-critical scenarios, prioritising brevity and immediate actionability.

items.name: Knowledge hub
items.body: Curated clinical knowledge retrieval with source attribution so clinicians can verify what they are reading.

items.name: Drug analytics
items.body: Interaction, usage, and reference analytics over drug data, built to surface caveats rather than final prescriptions.

items.name: Medical files
items.body: Ingestion and structured understanding of medical documents within the institution's own data boundary.

languages.title: Language set
languages.methodology: Declared planned interface language set in repository planning documentation.

steps.title: Clinician opens a case
steps.body: Context is entered or pulled from medical files inside the institution boundary.

steps.title: Assistant drafts support
steps.body: Differential prompts, consultation notes, and knowledge references — all attributed.

steps.title: Peer channel (optional)
steps.body: Doctor-to-doctor consult for a second licensed perspective.

steps.title: Clinician decides
steps.body: The licensed professional accepts, edits, or discards. No autonomous clinical action.

steps.title: Learning signal (anonymized)
steps.body: If consent and policy allow, de-identified signal feeds the anonymized learning pipeline.

ctaBand.title: Evaluate with your clinical informatics team
ctaBand.body: We walk the architecture diagram, the anonymization design, and the legal documentation — status labels intact.
